exact_claim: Dravidian speech has been present in the Brahui area of Balochistan continuously since a period substantially earlier than the Balochi expansion, and Brahui is a survival of that presence rather than an arrival into it.
chronological_fit: No retrieved source dates Dravidian speech in Balochistan at any period, in either direction. There is no chronological anchor to test this model against, so it neither passes nor fails a date check. Absence of a date is not a failed date check; constitution §6. The one dated frame retrieved is for Balochi, not Brahui: arrival from the northwest in waves between 1000 and 1500 AD (DMM-014), hedged by its own author as what is 'generally thought'. That dates the Iranian layer, not the Dravidian one.
geographical_fit: Plausible and untested. Constitution §4.M names highland refugia as a thing to investigate; nothing about Balochistan's highland zones was retrieved in this unit. Brahui's nearest attested Dravidian neighbour is 1,561.5 km away (DMB-010), which this model explains as a gap opened by loss in between and which every other model also explains.
mechanism: Continuous intergenerational transmission in situ, with the surrounding language landscape changing around it.
positive_evidence_retrieved: None that dates anything. DMM-005 - 260 of Brahui's 269 DEDR etymologies reach outside North Dravidian - is weakly consistent with early divergence, and is equally consistent with DMG-2, DMG-3 and DMG-5. It is not evidence for this model.
diagnostic_predictions: Would predict archaic retentions in Brahui not shared with Kurux and Malto; a substrate or adstrate signature in the regional Iranian languages from before the Balochi expansion; and an absence of any coherent migration-route vocabulary. None of the three was tested here.
what_would_gate_it: Krishnamurti 2003 on the North Dravidian innovations, so that Brahui's retentions can be separated from its innovations; Emeneau 1962; Elfenbein 1998; and any pre-nineteenth-century attestation of Brahui. HOLD-004, HOLD-005.
source_dependencies: Every source that would gate it is unread. See HOLD-004.
proportional_space: None in this unit. No model receives analytical space here, because none could be gated.
reason: Cannot be gated for want of sources, not failed. The chronological criterion cannot be applied at all because nothing retrieved dates Brahui's presence, and the positive-evidence criterion returns material that fits three other models equally well. This is the model the inherited record leans toward once late migration is rejected as a default (R-10), and that is precisely why it is not being advanced on an ungated basis here.

exact_claim: Brahui speakers migrated to Balochistan from a Dravidian-speaking region of the subcontinent at a comparatively late date, conventionally placed in the medieval period.
chronological_fit: No retrieved source dates Dravidian speech in Balochistan at any period, in either direction. There is no chronological anchor to test this model against, so it neither passes nor fails a date check. Absence of a date is not a failed date check; constitution §6. Constitution §4.M states in terms: do not treat medieval Brahui migration as documented fact. Nothing retrieved in this unit documents it. The source the inherited record carries as load-bearing for late migration, Elfenbein 1998, remains unread (IH-236).
geographical_fit: A route would have to be specified and none is. The nearest attested Dravidian language to Brahui is Kolami at 1,561.5 km, not Kurukh or Malto (DMB-011), so the geographic remainder does not itself suggest an origin point.
mechanism: Population movement carrying a language over long distance.
positive_evidence_retrieved: None for a medieval migration. One documented Brahui migration WAS retrieved (SRC-073: entry into Iranian Sistan and Balochistan within the last 400 years, and into southern Kerman about 200 years ago, from community oral literature and named local informants) - but it runs in the opposite direction, westward out of Pakistan, at a far later date, and it is community-authored material held at ledger level pending the rights steward (D-041). It is recorded here so that it is NOT quietly counted as support for a medieval eastward-to-westward migration. It is not.
contrary_evidence_retrieved: None retrieved. The absence of Brahui-specific exclusive sharing with Kurux and Malto (DMM-004) is sometimes read as telling against a shared northern origin, but a lexical null cannot carry that.
diagnostic_predictions: Would predict a traceable origin dialect within Dravidian, migration-period loans from languages along a route, and a shallow time depth for Brahui's divergence. None was tested here.
what_would_gate_it: Elfenbein 1998; Krishnamurti 2003; Emeneau 1962; and Korn 2005 read properly, so that the Balochi and Indo-Aryan strata in Brahui can be dated relative to each other. HOLD-004, HOLD-005.
reason: Cannot be gated for want of sources. This model carries a specific hazard the others do not: it is the one the constitution warns against treating as documented, the one PR #16 found built into the shape of the leave-one-out instrument (DMB-006), and the one the inherited record has already REJECTED as a default (R-10, IH-156, IH-031). Its being disfavoured is not a reason to gate it out either. It stands where the other five stand: ungated, for want of the same sources.

model: Broader ancient distribution followed by language replacement
exact_claim: Dravidian speech was formerly spoken over a substantially wider area than its attested modern range, including the northwest, and was replaced across most of that area, leaving Brahui as a remnant.
chronological_fit: No retrieved source dates Dravidian speech in Balochistan at any period, in either direction. There is no chronological anchor to test this model against, so it neither passes nor fails a date check. Absence of a date is not a failed date check; constitution §6. Replacement would have to be dated to a period, and the only replacement event with a retrieved date frame is the Balochi expansion (DMM-014), which is medieval and cannot by itself account for a distribution described as ancient.
geographical_fit: This model is the one that most directly requires unknown ancient Balochistan speech zones to stay unknown. What languages were spoken across Balochistan before the Iranian layer is not recoverable from anything retrieved here, and treating the modern attested Dravidian range as a sample of the ancient one is the error DMB-002 already identified.
mechanism: Language shift across a wide area under demographic, political or economic pressure, with survival at the margin.
positive_evidence_retrieved: None. DMM-005 is consistent with it and does not distinguish it from DMG-1 or DMG-5.
diagnostic_predictions: Would predict Dravidian substrate signatures in the languages that replaced it across the intervening zone, and toponymic residue. Neither was tested here; both are domain E and domain P work, and domain E's comparative half is itself on HOLD-002 and HOLD-003.
what_would_gate_it: A substrate study of the northwestern Indo-Aryan and Iranian languages against Dravidian comparanda, which requires DEDR in full plus the domain E sources; and Krishnamurti 2003. HOLD-002, HOLD-003, HOLD-004.
reason: Cannot be gated for want of sources. It is also the model most exposed to the negative-evidence standard: its central claim is about a distribution that has not survived, so it can only be argued from typed absences, and no absence in this unit has been typed in its favour.

model: Continuing dialect networks followed by fragmentation
exact_claim: Brahui, Kurukh and Malto are the surviving remnants of a dialect network that remained in contact across northern South Asia and later fragmented, rather than a clade that separated once from a common ancestor.
chronological_fit: No retrieved source dates Dravidian speech in Balochistan at any period, in either direction. There is no chronological anchor to test this model against, so it neither passes nor fails a date check. Absence of a date is not a failed date check; constitution §6. Fragmentation would need a date and none is retrievable.
geographical_fit: Would require a corridor across northern South Asia linking Balochistan to Chota Nagpur and the Rajmahal hills. Nothing retrieved evidences one.
mechanism: Prolonged contact and shared innovation across a chain of varieties, followed by the loss of the intervening links.
positive_evidence_retrieved: The one place the retrieved record touches this mechanism is DMM-011: Nair reports that the North Dravidian initial v-/b- change is not a shared innovation and may be a typologically motivated change under western and eastern Middle Indo-Aryan convergence, a reading attributed to Krishnamurti. That is an areal rather than a genealogical account of a North Dravidian feature - the shape this model predicts. But it concerns Kurux and Malto in contact with Middle Indo-Aryan, not Brahui, and one withdrawn isogloss is not a network.
contrary_evidence_retrieved: None retrieved. DMM-002's result - 176 exclusive Kurux-Malto sets against a null expectation of 0.71 - is often read as evidence for a clade, but as DMI-002 sets out, lexical exclusivity between neighbours cannot separate common descent from prolonged contact, so it does not tell against this model either.
diagnostic_predictions: Would predict features shared in overlapping rather than nested distributions, and innovations shared with non-Dravidian neighbours along the corridor. Testing needs phonological and morphological data this unit does not have.
what_would_gate_it: Krishnamurti 2003 on the North Dravidian innovations and their distributions; Kobayashi and Tirkey 2017 pp. 11-14; Nair 2003 read in full rather than at abstract level. HOLD-004.
reason: Cannot be gated for want of sources. Of the six it is the model best served by what WAS retrieved, because DMM-011 and DMM-010 together describe exactly the situation it predicts - a subgroup whose innovations are few, contested, and partly areal. That is a reason to gate it properly when the sources arrive, not a reason to advance it now.

model: Small migrating group plus extensive local language adoption
exact_claim: A small Dravidian-speaking group moved into or persisted in Balochistan, and the modern Brahui-speaking population is largely composed of local people who adopted the language, so that speaker ancestry and language history diverge sharply.
chronological_fit: No retrieved source dates Dravidian speech in Balochistan at any period, in either direction. There is no chronological anchor to test this model against, so it neither passes nor fails a date check. Absence of a date is not a failed date check; constitution §6.
geographical_fit: Consistent with any of the geographic facts retrieved and predicted by none of them.
mechanism: Language shift toward an incoming or persisting small group, with the linguistic and the demographic histories separating.
positive_evidence_retrieved: Nothing that dates or measures it. Two rows are consistent with it and neither is evidence for it. DMM-020: no signal of Oraon-related ancestry in the Brahui - which is what this model predicts, and which under the four-histories rule bears on speaker ancestry only and cannot be converted into a linguistic result (BF-008). DMM-019: Brahui kinship terms borrowed at the senior and affinal edges while core terms stay Dravidian - a contact profile compatible with this model and with every model involving long contact.
diagnostic_predictions: This is the model with the sharpest diagnostic, and it is the one this unit came closest to being able to test: it predicts that speaker ancestry and language history will NOT track each other, which is a testable divergence rather than a resemblance. Testing it properly needs both histories dated independently, and neither is dated here.
what_would_gate_it: A dated linguistic chronology for Brahui - which is HOLD-004's Krishnamurti 2003 and Elfenbein 1998 - set against the population-genetic literature read as ancestry and not as language. Neither half is available in the form required.
reason: Cannot be gated for want of sources. It needs its own warning: it is the model most easily 'confirmed' by genetic results, because a genetic null looks like its prediction. It is not confirmed by one. Genetics does not date a language, and a study that finds no Dravidian-related ancestry in the Brahui has measured ancestry, not adoption.

exact_claim: The history involves more than one of the five processes above - for example an older presence overlaid by a later movement, or fragmentation followed by local adoption.
chronological_fit: Not assessable as stated. A combination inherits the chronological requirements of each component, and none of the components has a chronology here.
mechanism: Two or more of the mechanisms above, in a specified order and at specified dates.
positive_evidence_retrieved: None. By construction this model is consistent with every observation that is consistent with any of its components, which is why it cannot be evidenced as it stands.
contrary_evidence_retrieved: None, and none is possible against it as stated.
diagnostic_predictions: None as stated. A combination makes diagnostic predictions only once its components, their order and their dates are fixed; until then it predicts whatever its components jointly allow.
what_would_gate_it: Decomposition first: the constitution requires this to be held open as one of six, and it is, but as a single row it cannot pass a step 7 gate, because a hypothesis that forbids no observation cannot be tested. What can be gated is a NAMED combination - for instance DMG-1 followed by DMG-5, with a date for the transition. Then the same sources that gate its components gate it.
source_dependencies: Inherits all of HOLD-004 and HOLD-005.
reason: Cannot be gated, and for a reason different in kind from the other five. They fail the gate for want of sources; this one is not yet a single hypothesis. It is held open as the constitution requires and it is flagged here as needing decomposition before it can ever receive analytical space - otherwise it becomes the residual that absorbs every result, which is the role constitution §6 forbids 'unknown' to play.
